entry.name: Wounded traveler in the Samaritan parable
entry.note: Unnamed man inside the story Jesus tells in Luke 10:30–35, traveling from Jerusalem to Jericho, stripped, beaten and left half dead. Distinct from the framing lawyer and from the Samaritan who helps him. Injuries and lost clothing are situational, not a separate life stage.

result.appearanceFromText: The text fixes only that he was a traveler stripped of his clothing, beaten and left half dead on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho; his age, build, face and dress are not described, so a typical Judean traveler of the Roman period is supplied, with his injuries kept situational and non-graphic.

stages.label: Wounded traveler
stages.when: Roman Judea, on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho

quotes.quote: A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him

stages.text: Wounded traveler: a man of about 30 to 45 years, of average build with a lean, weathered frame, olive skin, short dark hair and a close-cut beard. Facial features are plain and worn, marked with dust and bruising. Stripped to a simple loincloth of undyed linen, he has no cloak or sandals. Signature props: none, as robbers took his belongings.
